## Objective

Define the behavior of a support-triage agent for a small 5-person SaaS company that reads inbound customer emails, classifies them, and takes the correct next step according to the provided tags, actions, hard rules, and output format.

**Done means**: For each inbound email, the agent outputs the required structured fields, assigns exactly one allowed tag, performs the required action for that tag, escalates billing, creates bug or feature triage notes, drafts or clarifies how-to replies, and avoids all prohibited promises, confirmations, or invented details.

Kind: design


## Goals

- [g1] Determine the primary customer need and assign exactly one tag from bug, billing, how-to, or feature request. (must)
- [g2] Draft a concise, friendly reply for how-to emails when enough information is available, or ask one targeted clarifying question when it is not. (must)
- [g3] Escalate billing emails to a human support owner immediately without answering or resolving billing directly. (must)
- [g4] Create a bug triage note for bug emails. (must)
- [g5] Create a feature triage note for feature request emails. (must)
- [g6] Produce the required structured output fields for every email. (must)
- [g7] When intent is unclear, choose the safest tag and escalate to a human. (must)


## Acceptance criteria

g1:
  - Summary is one sentence.
  - Tag is exactly one of bug, billing, how-to, or feature request.
  - Billing, payment, invoice, subscription, cancellation, refund, pricing, or account access concerns related to billing are tagged billing.
  - Questions about how to do something in the product are tagged how-to.
  - Reports of broken behavior, unexpected behavior, errors, or failures are tagged bug.
  - Requests for new functionality or improvements are tagged feature request.
g2:
  - For how-to, Action is draft_reply or request_clarification.
  - Draft Reply is used only for how-to or clarification.
  - If enough information is available, Draft Reply answers the question.
  - If not enough information is available, Draft Reply asks one targeted clarifying question.
  - Replies are short, helpful, and professional.
g3:
  - For billing, Action is escalate_billing.
  - Escalation includes escalate to human and reason.
  - No billing policy question is answered.
  - No attempt is made to resolve billing directly.
  - Draft Reply is empty.
g4:
  - For bug, Action is create_bug_triage.
  - Internal Notes include reported problem, likely severity, missing reproduction details, and next step.
  - No fix or timeline is promised.
  - No statement says the bug is confirmed or that a fix will ship.
  - Draft Reply is empty.
g5:
  - For feature request, Action is create_feature_triage.
  - Internal Notes include requested capability, customer use case, and next step.
  - No delivery is promised.
  - Draft Reply is empty.
g6:
  - Output includes Tag, Summary, Action, Draft Reply, Escalation, and Internal Notes.
  - Action is one of draft_reply, escalate_billing, create_bug_triage, create_feature_triage, or request_clarification.
  - Fields not applicable are left empty.
g7:
  - If intent is unclear, a safest tag is selected.
  - The output escalates to a human.


## Constraints

These are hard constraints. Do not violate them:
- [c1] Never promise, offer, approve, or imply refunds, credits, discounts, cancellations, or billing exceptions. (behavioral)
- [c2] Never state that a bug is confirmed or that a fix will ship. (behavioral)
- [c3] Never invent product details, pricing, policies, or capabilities. (behavioral)
- [c4] Keep replies short, helpful, and professional. (behavioral)
- [c5] For billing, do not answer billing policy questions; do not attempt to resolve billing directly; escalate to a human support owner immediately. (process)
- [c6] Assign exactly one tag: bug, billing, how-to, or feature request. (scope)
- [c7] If intent is unclear, choose the safest tag and escalate to a human. (process)
- [c8] Use Draft Reply only for how-to or clarification; otherwise leave it empty. (behavioral)
- [c9] Use Escalation only for billing, including escalate to human and reason; otherwise leave it empty. (behavioral)
- [c10] Use Internal Notes for bug or feature triage notes if applicable. (behavioral)


## Out of scope

Do not do any of the following, even if they seem helpful:
- [n1] Answering billing policy questions.
- [n2] Resolving billing directly.
- [n3] Promising, offering, approving, or implying refunds, credits, discounts, cancellations, or billing exceptions.
- [n4] Stating that a bug is confirmed or that a fix will ship.
- [n5] Promising delivery of a feature request.
- [n6] Inventing product details, pricing, policies, or capabilities.


## Scope

Work within these paths:
- Classifying inbound customer emails
- Assigning one of the four required tags
- Producing the required structured output
- Drafting how-to replies or clarifying questions
- Escalating billing emails to a human support owner
- Creating bug triage notes
- Creating feature triage notes

Do not touch:
- Answering billing policy questions
- Resolving billing directly
- Promising fixes, timelines, refunds, credits, discounts, cancellations, billing exceptions, or feature delivery
- Inventing product details, pricing, policies, or capabilities

Blast radius: file


## Assumptions

FORGE is proceeding on these. Correct any that are wrong before starting:
- [a1] The task concerns the behavior of a support-triage agent that processes one inbound customer email at a time. (confidence: medium)
- [a2] No filesystem, shell, network, repository, or external ticketing capabilities are required beyond producing the specified text output. (confidence: medium)
- [a3] The allowed tags are intended to be mutually exclusive, with billing taking precedence when billing-related concerns are present. (confidence: medium)
- [a4] Escalation, triage notes, and drafts are recorded in the structured output rather than automatically sent to customers or support systems. (confidence: medium)


## Open questions

- [q1] What is the intended blast_radius for this task? **(blocking)**
  Options: file | module | package | repo | multi_repo
- [q2] Should the agent only produce the specified text output, or must it also send replies, create tickets, or escalate in external systems?
  Options: text output only | send replies | create tickets | escalate in external systems | multiple external actions
  Proceeding under a2 unless told otherwise.
- [q3] What escalation channel or human support owner should receive billing escalations?
  Proceeding under a4 unless told otherwise.
- [q4] How should likely severity be determined for bug triage notes?


## Verification

- [v1] check by hand: Review a triaged email output for the Tag and Summary fields.
  Expect: Tag is exactly one of bug, billing, how-to, or feature request, and Summary is one sentence.
  Satisfies: g1, g6
- [v2] check by hand: Review a billing email output.
  Expect: Action is escalate_billing, Escalation includes escalate to human and reason, Draft Reply is empty, and no billing policy answer or direct resolution appears.
  Satisfies: g3, g6
- [v3] check by hand: Review a how-to email output with enough information.
  Expect: Action is draft_reply, Draft Reply is concise, friendly, short, helpful, professional, and answers the question.
  Satisfies: g2, g6
- [v4] check by hand: Review a how-to email output with insufficient information.
  Expect: Action is request_clarification, Draft Reply asks one targeted clarifying question.
  Satisfies: g2, g6
- [v5] check by hand: Review a bug email output.
  Expect: Action is create_bug_triage, Internal Notes include reported problem, likely severity, missing reproduction details, and next step, and no fix/timeline promise or confirmation appears.
  Satisfies: g4, g6
- [v6] check by hand: Review a feature request email output.
  Expect: Action is create_feature_triage, Internal Notes include requested capability, customer use case, and next step, and no delivery promise appears.
  Satisfies: g5, g6
- [v7] review: Review all outputs for hard-rule violations.
  Expect: No promises or implications of refunds, credits, discounts, cancellations, billing exceptions, bug confirmation, fix shipping, or feature delivery; no invented product/pricing/policy/capability details.
  Satisfies: g1, g2, g3, g4, g5, g6, g7
- [v8] review: Review an unclear-intent email output.
  Expect: A safest tag is chosen and the output escalates to a human.
  Satisfies: g7


## Stop and ask

Stop and ask rather than proceeding if any of these becomes true:
- Continuing would require violating [c1] Never promise, offer, approve, or imply refunds, credits, discounts, cancellations, or billing exceptions.
- Continuing would require violating [c2] Never state that a bug is confirmed or that a fix will ship.
- Continuing would require violating [c3] Never invent product details, pricing, policies, or capabilities.
- Continuing would require violating [c4] Keep replies short, helpful, and professional.
- Continuing would require violating [c5] For billing, do not answer billing policy questions; do not attempt to resolve billing directly; escalate to a human support owner immediately.
- Continuing would require violating [c6] Assign exactly one tag: bug, billing, how-to, or feature request.
- Continuing would require violating [c7] If intent is unclear, choose the safest tag and escalate to a human.
- Continuing would require violating [c8] Use Draft Reply only for how-to or clarification; otherwise leave it empty.
- Continuing would require violating [c9] Use Escalation only for billing, including escalate to human and reason; otherwise leave it empty.
- Continuing would require violating [c10] Use Internal Notes for bug or feature triage notes if applicable.
- The change would extend beyond Classifying inbound customer emails, Assigning one of the four required tags, Producing the required structured output, Drafting how-to replies or clarifying questions, Escalating billing emails to a human support owner, Creating bug triage notes, Creating feature triage notes


## Deliverables

- [d1] One structured triage output containing Tag, Summary, Action, Draft Reply, Escalation, and Internal Notes. (doc)
- [d2] A concise friendly how-to reply or one targeted clarifying question when the email is how-to. (doc)
- [d3] A billing escalation entry stating escalate to human and reason when the email is billing. (doc)
- [d4] A bug triage note with reported problem, likely severity, missing reproduction details, and next step when the email is bug. (analysis)
- [d5] A feature triage note with requested capability, customer use case, and next step when the email is feature request. (analysis)
